glyhub

glyhub collects glycomics and glycoproteomics data for the Glycoverse ecosystem, using the GlycomicSE and GlycoproteomicSE containers from glyexp. The package is experimental.

Available data

75 datasets from 47 public GlycoPOST projects are available, including released glycans, glycosaminoglycan disaccharides and site/charge-resolved glycopeptides. Objects combine source-defined quantitative tables from the same study and glycan class where measurement definitions are compatible. GPST000602 is explicitly an annotated-peak subset with spectrum-specific, unaligned feature identities. Inclusion does not imply recovery of every experiment in its paper.

Each dataset has its own help page describing the biological system, experimental design, units, source table and limitations. Use glyhub_catalog() for the complete catalog. N/O classes remain separate; source experiments, sample conditions and replicate labels remain in colData. Feature unions use documented author keys or supported structures, with an explicit source-coverage mask for unmeasured combinations.

For GlycoPOST datasets, zero-valued abundances are stored as NA in the distributed assays. Original values, source-missing values and conflict masks remain in metadata. No imputation or renormalization is applied. Unknown molecular annotations remain NA without removing quantitative rows. Structures are encoded only from explicit source structural evidence. Unresolved bonds and attachment positions remain uncertain.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("glycoverse/glyhub")

Example 

x <- glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1")
dim(x)
data.frame(as.list(S4Vectors::metadata(x)$processing_counts))

All datasets use glyhub_load(). SummarizedExperiment::assay(x) contains the curated abundance matrix; S4Vectors::metadata(x)$raw_abundance preserves the unconverted values. rowData(x) retains typed glyrepr annotations and source evidence, and colData(x) retains source conditions and observation locations.

Loading external data

The 83 existing released datasets are stored in the Glyhub data release. The package includes the catalog and loader code, with no bundled data objects. Thirteen non-CPTAC datasets are available in the existing data release. Eight have explicit PRIDE CC0 source-file licenses. For the human atlas, mouse brain, lung and two HCC objects, source-license scope remains unresolved; publication does not establish or grant a new license. See the per-object source and publication records.

head(glyhub::glyhub_catalog()[, c("dataset", "source", "bytes")])
#>                       dataset    source  bytes
#> 1 glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1 GlycoPOST  85324
#> 2 glyhub_GPST000738_N_ST6GAL1 GlycoPOST  86980
#> 3         glyhub_GPST000643_O GlycoPOST 136920
#> 4         glyhub_GPST000643_N GlycoPOST  10320
#> 5         glyhub_GPST000213_N GlycoPOST 273048
#> 6         glyhub_GPST000213_O GlycoPOST  46920

Use either the common loader or a dataset’s own function. Both share the same verified cache and return the same object:

x <- glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC")
x <- glyhub::glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC()

x <- glyhub::glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1()
x <- glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1", offline = TRUE)

# Original CPTAC source archive; returns a verified local file path.
raw_file <- glyhub::glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC(kind = "raw")
# Equivalent: glyhub::glyhub_load("glyhub_CPTAC_CCRCC", kind = "raw")

Breaking interface change: all former dataset objects are now functions. Add () when using a dataset name directly, or pass its name to glyhub_load(). LazyData, variable-style access and data() access are no longer provided. glyhub_catalog() lists all curated datasets; kind = "raw" lists available source archives, currently the eight CPTAC archives. Dataset help topics retain scientific details and source references.

Every resource is checked against its size and SHA-256 before use. For released resources, the first call requires an internet connection; subsequent calls reuse the cache. Set cache_dir or option glyhub.cache_dir to select its location. refresh = TRUE retrieves the pinned version again; offline = TRUE prohibits downloads and requires a valid cached file. Delete cached files to clear the cache.

Non-CPTAC studies

These datasets prefer deposited reporter intensities, chromatographic peak areas, or the authors’ raw expression matrices. Source zeros are preserved. No additional normalization, imputation, logarithm, or inverse transformation is applied.

glyhub_PXD052447_N_Tissues() contains 205,904 deposited PSM rows across 18 TMT channels from three tissues of two mice, with technical replication. PSM rows are not unique glycopeptides. Rows without glycan annotations and unused or unmapped channels remain explicitly identifiable in the source annotations. Measurement channels and technical runs are not automatically independent people or animals.

Some studies provide only processed quantitative tables. Their help pages and metadata state the scale, source normalization, transformations, imputation and feature selection. In particular, the HCC discovery table contains selected features, so it is not suitable for unbiased feature discovery or classifier performance estimation. metadata(x)$raw_abundance preserves source numbers; it does not imply that a processed source table is raw intensity. The earliest unnormalized HCC clinical matrix was not available through the inspected sources; the linear QC table represents a different experiment and cannot replace it.

See the source-selection audit and rebuild instructions. Data licenses remain separate from the package’s code license. PRIDE CC0 evidence applies to the eight DQGlyco/Glyco-DIA objects, not automatically to publisher supplements or the five objects with unresolved source-license scope. Original sources, attribution, processing and limitations remain in each object’s metadata and the publication records.
